The Akhtyrka Icon of the Theotokos

Icons

Theotokos

The Akhtyrka Icon of the Theotokos

Akhtyr · Akhtyrskaya

What is depictedHistory and traditionPublished explanationSources

The Akhtyrka tradition centres on the Mother of God beside Christ’s Cross and the icon found by the priest Basil Danilov in 1739.

[1] Opening discovery

What is depicted

The selected eighteenth-century image presents Mary with crossed hands beside a smaller Crucifixion. Her covered head and the arrangement of the hands belong to this displayed example. It is a reproduction of a specific old Akhtyrka-type panel; later copies need not repeat every detail of the particular original described by a commemorative article.

[2] Displayed work;file-level title,description,date and visual identification

History and tradition

The OCA recounts the discovery in grass near the church and a series of healing stories after the icon was cleaned. It records repeated investigations, a 1751 Synodal recognition and a stone church funded with Empress Elizabeth’s support. The church was consecrated in 1768. These are attributed events and religious testimonies within the source’s shrine history.

[1] Discovery,investigations and church

Published explanation

The OCA expressly notes Western stylistic features in the original it describes and says that original is not the image displayed on its page. That distinction matters for copies: the uncovered head or specific prayer gesture mentioned there cannot automatically be assigned to every Akhtyrka reproduction. Its printed July 2 commemoration is retained without creating a civil-date conversion.

[1] Iconographic paragraph and date
